conventions.convention: The vertex rotation σ is clockwise; the face permutation is α∘σ, applying σ first. A plane code additionally selects one face as its outer face.

Positive and negative Gauss visits mean over and under, respectively; algebraic crossing signs are separate data. Crossing sign is the sign of det(v_over,v_under) in the plane oriented by the viewing normal. A positive normalized clockwise crossing is (O_out,U_in,O_in,U_out).

Nonempty crossing graphs must be connected. Separate crossingless components and disconnected crossing graphs are excluded. At zero crossings only one circle is admitted, with a cw or ccw orientation marker and outer-face marker outside.
Signed DT entries pair odd visits with distinct even visits; an entry is positive exactly when its odd visit is over. A separate algebraic crossing-sign vector is required.

Normalized codes fix crossing labels, begin each clockwise crossing record at its outgoing over-dart, assign edge labels by first occurrence in the crossing/dart scan, and identify the selected face by its least dart. Crossing relabelings may still duplicate candidates.
Finite realization and enumeration are choice-free; Countable Choice is assumed for smooth ambient-isotopy uniqueness.

load_bearing.statement: Defines finite oriented dart codes, clockwise crossing rotations, edge pairings, separate over/under and algebraic signs, spherical face validation, selected outer faces, normalized PD records, Gauss and signed DT formats, and the separate oriented crossingless-circle case.

For a nonempty connected crossing code satisfying the prescribed local over/under, arrow, and sign-consistent cyclic-order conditions, a spherical realization exists if and only if V−E+F=2, with F the number of cycles of α∘σ. Selecting an outer face gives a plane realization; the crossingless one-component case is handled separately.

For every finite input in the three code formats, validation and reconstruction terminate, return the first failed prescribed condition when one fails, and otherwise return the represented oriented diagram's crossing-disk/edge-band model, components, face cycles, and selected outer face.

For every nonnegative integer N, bounded enumeration terminates and returns exactly the reconstructed candidates represented by normalized connected one-component planar-diagram codes with at most N crossings, without identifying repeated knot types.
Every finite nonempty connected polygonal plane multigraph, allowing loops and parallel edges and counting complementary components as faces, satisfies V−E+F=2.
